clue.text: You couldn't really call a sandwich this

definitions.text: You couldn't really call a sandwich this

parts.words: You couldn't really call a sandwich this
parts.note: a sandwich is only a snack, so it falls short of a proper, filling, nourishing dinner; the phrase hides a pun on a square-cut sandwich

explanation.surface: A remark that a mere sandwich hardly counts as a proper meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper, substantial, nourishing meal is what this idiom names, and a snack does not qualify.

clue.text: Ends up as only a brief fall of rain

definitions.text: only a brief fall of rain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tips are ends

explanation.surface: Something turns out to be merely a short shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit is to rain lightly in a few scattered drops, a short sprinkle.

clue.text: Jim wasn't jinxed

parts.note: un- is the negating prefix, saying the name that follows is not so
Lucky Jim is Kingsley Amis's 1954 comic novel, so Jim is lucky

explanation.surface: A man named Jim was not under a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucky Jim, a famous English comic novel, makes Jim 'lucky'; if he wasn't, he was the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jinxed is dogged by bad luck, so ill-starred is a synonym.

clue.text: City in which I travelled around with girl — I travelled half-way

indicators.note: around means going round, so the word for travelled encloses the single letter

parts.note: rode means travelled, on horseback or by vehicle
Jane is a girl's name

indicators.note: half-way says only the first half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: rode again means travelled

explanation.surface: A traveller's story of touring a city with a girl, getting only halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: This Brazilian metropolis is a large city, a specific example.

clue.text: If I'd more change, I could provide change…

indicators.note: change, the first one, means alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that with more coins they could give change.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cash; the second 'change' means alteration, as a qualifying word alters another.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a qualifying word alters the meaning of another, so it effects change.

clue.text: …. for a fellow without the right silver

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the fellow goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: change for a man who lacks the correct silver coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots continue 4 Down's 'change'. 'without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside; argent is silver in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry argent is the tincture representing the metal of that colour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Talk about the right clothes

indicators.note: about here means going round the outside, so the talk word wraps the letter for right

parts.note: gab is chatter, idle talk

explanation.surface: Someone discusses what the correct outfit is to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the right clothes' reads as one phrase, but 'right' is the letter R and 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or attire, a synonym.

clue.text: All right, I'll go round it quickly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: go round means encircle, so the self word surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: I is the ego, the self; the 'll is a link

explanation.surface: Someone agrees and promises to circle it fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All right' looks like a phrase of agreement; it splits into ALL and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction meaning at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Saw what boy scouts should do

definitions.meaning: the motto of the Scout movement

explanation.surface: A proverb about how Scouts ought to behave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scout motto is a well-known saying, and it tells Scouts to stay ready.

clue.text: Here in London one's golf does go to pieces

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds an S, giving IS

indicators.note: to go to pieces is to fall apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone's golf game collapses in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange I and S with GOLF and DOES; the result is a district of East London on a Thames peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: This peninsula in the East End is a district within London, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Friends about to come to blows

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Friends are on the point of starting a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the turning signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone with an open hand is a way of starting a fight, a loose verbal equivalent.

clue.text: Frontier character who broke out of many a jail, etc

indicators.note: breaking out suggests things smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outlaw of the Wild West who escaped from numerous prisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha Jane Canary was a famous Wild West frontierswoman known by this nickname.

clue.text: Area covered by a port

definitions.meaning: a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards
An ancient port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A stretch of land within a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The land unit and the Israeli harbour town share this spelling, giving two senses.

clue.text: Elaborate ornament for devoted admirer to hold out as temptation

parts.note: a fan is a devoted admirer
to dangle something is to hold it out as a lure

explanation.surface: A fancy trinket offered by a fan as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandangle is a fussy, showy decoration or gewgaw, a synonym.

clue.text: A roller, perhaps, has chalked this on the hillside

definitions.meaning: a big foam-crested wave rolling to shore

definitions.text: has chalked this on the hillside
definitions.meaning: a figure of a steed cut into chalk downland, as at Uffington in England

explanation.surface: A breaking wave and the chalk figure carved on an English hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam-topped breakers and the ancient chalk-cut steed figures of southern England share this name.

clue.text: Punch still working on some farms

definitions.meaning: a powerful swinging blow with the fist
a farmhand who cuts and dries grass for fodder, still employed in places

explanation.surface: A blow still dealt by labourers on certain farms.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild swinging blow and a farm labourer turning cut grass both carry this name.

clue.text: State confines a deity in a temple

indicators.note: confines means encloses, so the state's letters go round the rest

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: A government restricts a god to a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu shrine, a kind of sacred building.

clue.text: Firm — one.I'll leave this month

annotationWithheld.why: Firm — one I'll leave this month: CO (firm) + INSTANT (this month) less I gives the letters, but 'Firm' must then also be the definition, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Breaking a steel comb

indicators.note: breaking means smashing up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A metal comb snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The dried, spiny flower head of this plant was used to raise the nap on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Its prickly seed heads were used to card or tease cloth, so it serves as a comb.

clue.text: Diplomat can thus make them subject

annotationWithheld.why: Diplomat can thus make them subject: no parse found that builds the letters from 'can thus make them subject'; the wordplay is unclear
annotationWithheld.clue: Diplomat can thus make them subject

clue.text: Put up bird in minute cover

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the bird goes within the written record

parts.note: a minute is a short written record, a note
the mina (myna) is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Housing a bird inside a tiny shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is a link that also hints at the note wrapping the bird; 'minute' is a memo, not tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up for office is to propose them as a candidate, the same sense.

clue.text: Split — see below

definitions.meaning: as two words, the formal phrase '...' means as set out below

explanation.surface: A broken item, with a pointer to further notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart describes something divided; read as two words it is the document phrase directing readers lower down.

clue.text: Spirit, provided that it turns up in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from the bottom, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: élan is spirit, dash
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A spirit appears at last, provided that it shows itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses ELAN plus IF together, giving FI then NALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its conclusion.

clue.text: Most Irish are disorganized and casual

indicators.note: disorganized means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweeping claim that the Irish are chaotic and offhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a haphazard, random way is careless, a synonym.

clue.text: The familiar part of Tokyo, urban at heart

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A familiar district at the centre of the city of Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' adds that the letters sit in the middle of TokYO URban. Colloquially 'your' stands for 'the' in phrases like 'your average voter'.
explanation.definitionFit: In casual speech 'your' replaces 'the' to mean typical or ordinary, as in 'your everyday tourist'.

clue.text: Carriage -. governor of Paris is without one

indicators.note: is without means lacks, so a letter is taken out of the king's name

parts.note: Priam, king of Troy, was father of Paris and so the head of his household
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A carriage the mayor of Paris lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'governor of Paris' suggests the French capital; Paris is the Trojan prince, son of King Priam. 'governor' is old slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a baby carriage, a pushchair on wheels.

clue.text: People in the event

definitions.meaning: a nation or ethnic group of people
a contest of speed, such as a sprint

explanation.surface: Competitors taking part in a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A group sharing ancestry and a speed contest are both named by this word.

clue.text: One who can stand fire, soldier wearing a helmet, right?

indicators.note: something wearing a helmet is inside it, so the soldier goes within the headgear

parts.note: a salade (sallet) is a light medieval helmet
man is a common word for a soldier, as in men under arms

explanation.surface: A helmeted soldier who can face enemy fire, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: Legend held this amphibian could live in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard-like amphibian was fabled to survive in flames, and the word also means someone unafraid of gunfire.

clue.text: Still of the night

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning yet more, as in 'still better'
the poetic noun for the close of the day

explanation.surface: The quiet of nighttime.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning 'yet more' as in 'better yet', and as an old poetic noun the evening.

clue.text: Before the soirée, the Captain is to be found in the kitchen

definitions.text: Before the soirée, the Captain is to be found in the kitchen

parts.words: Before the soirée, the Captain is to be found in the kitchen
parts.note: an old word for a large afternoon tea party, held before the evening soirée; Captain Kettle was a popular fictional hero, and a kettle is found in the kitchen

explanation.surface: A naval captain spends the afternoon in the kitchen before an evening party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian term for a large afternoon tea gathering, preceding an evening reception.
